overview: Add a first-class `smithctl config` command group so operators can manage local Smith CLI contexts directly instead of editing `~/.smith/config.json` by hand. The first version should cover the full local config lifecycle for contexts, preserve compatibility with existing global flags and environment variables, and present configuration in YAML-oriented output suited to operator inspection.
goals: Provide a dedicated `smithctl config` command group for viewing and managing local CLI configuration.
Support the core context lifecycle expected from a kubectl-like CLI: inspect contexts, see the current context, switch contexts, and manage context records.
Allow direct field updates for context `server` and `token` values through CLI commands instead of manual JSON edits.
Create the config file automatically on write operations when `~/.smith/config.json` does not yet exist.
Keep existing `--config`, `--context`, `--server`, `--token`, and environment-variable behavior intact so the new commands complement the current resolution model.
nonGoals: OS keychain, secret store, or encrypted credential integration.
Interactive prompts, TUI editing flows, or wizard-style setup.
Import/export/merge support for kubeconfig-style or external config formats.
Shell completion, editor integration, or broader CLI UX redesign beyond the `config` command group.
Changing non-config commands to require the new `config` subcommands before existing flags or environment variables work.
successMetrics: An operator can create, inspect, switch, update, and delete Smith CLI contexts without hand-editing JSON files.
Write operations succeed against an empty workstation by creating `~/.smith/config.json` automatically.
Existing non-config `smithctl` commands continue to resolve config correctly from file, env vars, and flags after the feature lands.
Config command behavior is covered by focused `cmd/smithctl` tests and the feature passes the required Go test and lint gates.
openQuestions: Should YAML output be the default only for `smithctl config` commands or should this feature also extend the global `--output` flag beyond `text|json`?
Should token values be fully displayed in YAML output, partially redacted, or controllable with an explicit reveal flag in a later iteration?
Should `delete-context` be allowed to remove the current context directly, or must users switch away first?

stack.auth: Existing bearer token model stored in config file and overridden by environment variables or command-line flags

routes.name: Config View
routes.purpose: Display config data in YAML-oriented output for operator inspection.

routes.name: Context List
routes.purpose: List configured contexts and identify the current context.

routes.name: Set Context
routes.purpose: Create or update a named context record.

routes.name: Delete Context
routes.purpose: Remove a named context from the local config.

routes.name: Rename Context
routes.purpose: Rename an existing context while preserving its values.

uiNotes: Command help output should present `config` alongside the existing top-level resources.
YAML output should be stable and readable for operator use and scripting, especially for `view` and `get-contexts`.
Read commands should produce sensible empty-state output when no config file exists instead of failing with file-not-found errors.
Write commands should surface precise, actionable errors for invalid arguments, duplicate names, unknown contexts, and invalid rename/delete operations.

importFormat.description: Not applicable. The feature manages the existing local JSON config file format and adds YAML-oriented display output for CLI commands.

rules: The feature applies to the existing codebase in this repository.
The `config` command group complements existing global flags and environment variables; it does not replace them.
Read operations must tolerate a missing config file and return empty/default state rather than failing.
Write operations must create the parent config directory and `config.json` file automatically when missing.
Context names must be explicit CLI operands and validated for non-empty values.
Set/update commands must support direct mutation of `server` and `token` fields for a named context.
The current-context pointer must remain valid after write operations or fail with a clear error when an operation would leave it invalid.
Output for config inspection commands should be YAML-oriented for the first version.
The feature must preserve config resolution precedence already used by non-config commands: config file values, then environment overrides, then explicit flags.

stories.title: Add config command scaffolding
stories.description: As an operator, I want `smithctl` to expose a `config` command group so that configuration management is a first-class CLI workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: `smithctl help` lists `config` as a top-level command alongside the existing resources.
`smithctl config` without a subcommand prints command-specific help and exits successfully.
The implementation reuses the existing config file structs and parsing model rather than introducing a parallel config representation.
Example: running `smithctl config` prints usage for subcommands such as `view`, `get-contexts`, and `use-context`.
Negative case: running `smithctl config unknown` exits non-zero and prints a clear unknown-command error.

stories.title: View config in YAML form
stories.description: As an operator, I want to inspect my Smith CLI configuration in YAML-oriented output so that I can understand the current local state quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: `smithctl config view` prints the local config in YAML-oriented output derived from the existing config structure.
The command supports inspecting the config file even when no current context is set.
Example: with a config containing `default` and `staging`, `smithctl config view` emits YAML showing `current_context` and both contexts.
Negative case: if the config file is missing, `smithctl config view` succeeds and returns an empty/default YAML structure instead of failing.

stories.title: List and report current context
stories.description: As an operator, I want to list contexts and query the current context so that I can tell which Smith API target I am pointed at.
acceptanceCriteria: `smithctl config get-contexts` lists all defined contexts and identifies the current one.
`smithctl config current-context` prints the active context name when one is set.
Example: if `current_context` is `staging`, `smithctl config current-context` returns `staging` and `get-contexts` marks it as current.
Negative case: if no config file or current context exists, `current-context` exits non-zero with a clear message or returns an explicit empty-state result as defined by the implementation.

stories.title: Switch active context
stories.description: As an operator, I want to switch the active Smith CLI context so that subsequent commands target a different server without repeated flags.
acceptanceCriteria: `smithctl config use-context <name>` updates `current_context` in the config file.
The command preserves all existing context records and only changes the active pointer.
Example: running `smithctl config use-context staging` changes `current_context` from `default` to `staging`.
Negative case: using an unknown context name exits non-zero and does not modify the config file.

stories.title: Create and update contexts
stories.description: As an operator, I want to create or update context records from the CLI so that I do not have to edit config JSON manually.
acceptanceCriteria: `smithctl config set-context <name> --server URL --token TOKEN` creates a new named context or updates an existing one.
Write commands automatically create `~/.smith/config.json` and any missing parent directories if they do not exist.
Field updates support `server` and `token` values on the named context.
Example: on a fresh machine with no config file, `smithctl config set-context default --server http://127.0.0.1:8080 --token abc` creates the file with the named context.
Negative case: providing an empty context name or omitting all mutable fields exits non-zero and does not write a partial config file.

stories.title: Rename and delete contexts safely
stories.description: As an operator, I want to rename or delete obsolete contexts so that local Smith CLI configuration stays maintainable over time.
acceptanceCriteria: `smithctl config rename-context <old> <new>` renames an existing context and preserves its fields.
`smithctl config delete-context <name>` removes the named context from the config.
If the current context is renamed, the current-context pointer is updated to the new name.
Example: renaming `staging` to `preprod` preserves the same `server` and `token` values under the new key.
Negative case: deleting or renaming an unknown context exits non-zero and does not modify the config file.

stories.title: Preserve runtime resolution compatibility
stories.description: As an operator, I want existing `smithctl` command resolution behavior to remain compatible so that adding config commands does not break current automation.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing global flags (`--config`, `--context`, `--server`, `--token`) continue to work for non-config commands after the feature lands.
Environment-variable overrides (`SMITH_API_URL`, `SMITH_OPERATOR_TOKEN`, `SMITH_CONTEXT`) continue to override file-backed context values as they do today.
Example: after setting a default context in the config file, `SMITH_API_URL=http://override smithctl loop list` still targets the override URL.
Negative case: adding config subcommands does not change the result of existing config resolution tests for unrelated `loop` or `prd` commands.

stories.title: Cover config workflows with focused tests
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want focused automated coverage for the new config workflows so that the CLI remains stable as config behavior grows.
acceptanceCriteria: Add or extend `cmd/smithctl` tests to cover view, get-contexts, current-context, use-context, set-context, rename-context, and delete-context behavior.
Tests cover both missing-file behavior for reads and auto-create behavior for writes.
Example: a test creates a temp config path, runs `set-context`, and verifies the file contents and current-context behavior.
Negative case: tests assert non-zero exit codes and unchanged file state for unknown contexts, invalid arguments, and invalid write requests.
The feature passes `mise exec --no-prepare -- go test ./cmd/smithctl` and `mise exec --no-prepare -- go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/cmd/golangci-lint@v1.64.8 run ./...`.
